correctness.rationale: For equal outputs on two binary inputs, their integer difference h satisfies h(a)=-h(b) on every edge. Connectivity forces an alternating constant in each component; an odd cycle forces zero. In a nontrivial bipartite component a nonzero difference has magnitude one and is feasible only between the two complementary proper colorings. Hence on that component exactly one fiber has size two and the other 2^v−2 have size one; an isolate contributes one size-two fiber; the nonbipartite part contributes 2^u singleton fibers. Cartesian products of observations multiply fiber sizes, proving the polynomial. Its lowest nonzero degree and leading coefficient recover s and 2^u; after division the roots recover all v with multiplicity. F(1) counts outputs, F(2)=2^|V| counts inputs, and the top degree s+b and coefficient 2^u give the maximum size and its multiplicity. Normalizing the largest fiber by 2^|V| gives the stated entropy. Empty graph, edgeless graphs, and no-nontrivial-bipartite cases all follow, with F=1 on the empty vertex set. Independent bit-mask enumeration of both approximations on all 1100 labeled graphs of orders 0 through 5 agreed with the product (python3 /workspace/reproductions/enumerator_review.py). The frozen script's stated total 33867 exhausts positive orders 1–6, not order zero; this imprecise wording about a finite check does not change the theorem or its empty-graph proof.

value.rationale: The full ambiguity distribution, without vertex labels or even the graph order as side information, exactly separates recoverable component-order data from unrecoverable topology. For example, one connected nonbipartite graph of order six and two disjoint triangles give the same spectrum even though their component counts differ. Neither the maximum fiber alone nor an injectivity test supplies this classification. The result is uniform over arbitrary finite graphs, and the entropy and hyperedge boundary make the limits of the observation model precise.
